Bayesian occurrence-abundance microbiome estimation (MaAsLin3-compatible)

Source: R/bayome.R
bayome.Rd

Main entry point of bayome. The arguments follow maaslin3::maaslin3() so that an existing MaAsLin3 call can be reused by changing only the function name. Bayesian settings are optional extras.

Usage

bayome(
  input_data,
  input_metadata = NULL,
  output = NULL,
  formula = NULL,
  fixed_effects = NULL,
  reference = NULL,
  random_effects = NULL,
  group_effects = NULL,
  ordered_effects = NULL,
  strata_effects = NULL,
  min_abundance = 0,
  min_prevalence = 0,
  max_prevalence = 1.01,
  zero_threshold = 0,
  min_variance = 0,
  max_significance = 0.1,
  normalization = c("TSS", "CLR", "NONE"),
  transform = c("LOG", "PLOG", "NONE"),
  standardize = TRUE,
  evaluate_only = NULL,
  prior = bm_prior(),
  link = c("none", "shared"),
  shrinkage = c("joint", "none", "hierarchical"),
  exposure = NULL,
  hierarchical_reference = c("mean", "median"),
  hierarchical_variance = c("vb", "plugin", "estimated"),
  int_strategy = c("auto", "ccd", "grid", "eb"),
  median_comparison_abundance = TRUE,
  median_comparison_prevalence = FALSE,
  median_comparison_abundance_threshold = 0,
  median_comparison_prevalence_threshold = 0,
  subtract_median = FALSE,
  n_draws = 4000,
  selection = c("bh_lfsr", "rope", "lfsr"),
  rope_delta = 0.5,
  save_models = FALSE,
  cores = 1,
  verbosity = "FINEST",
  ...
)

Arguments

input_data

Feature table (data frame or matrix). Samples may be in rows or columns; they are matched to input_metadata by name.

input_metadata

Metadata data frame with samples in rows.

output

Output directory for all_results.tsv and significant_results.tsv, or NULL to write nothing.

formula

One-sided formula or string in MaAsLin3 notation, e.g. ~ diagnosis + age + ordered(stage) + (1 | subject).

fixed_effects, random_effects, group_effects, ordered_effects, strata_effects

Alternative to formula, as in maaslin3(). Ignored if formula is given.

reference

Reference levels, as in maaslin3(), e.g. "diagnosis,nonIBD" or c("diagnosis,nonIBD", "site,A").

min_abundance, min_prevalence, max_prevalence, zero_threshold, min_variance

Feature filtering thresholds, as in maaslin3().

max_significance

Threshold on qval_individual / qval_joint for significant_results.tsv.

normalization, transform

Pre-processing, as in maaslin3().

standardize

Z-score continuous metadata used as fixed effects.

evaluate_only

NULL (both parts), "abundance" or "prevalence".

prior

Priors, see bm_prior().

link

"none" (separate random effects per part) or "shared" (abundance random intercepts are a scaled copy of the prevalence ones).

shrinkage

How information is shared across features and between the two parts:

  • "joint" (default): one INLA model with both parts and all features. Prevalence: one effect per feature, u_P ~ N(0, 2.5^2) (fixed, no pooling). Abundance: u_A = lambda * u_P + e, where lambda (one per covariate, N(0, 1) prior) links abundance to prevalence and e ~ N(0, 1/tau) is shared across features (PC prior on tau). This structure is used for the exposure only; the other covariates (adjustment covariates) get one effect per feature and part with a fixed N(0, 2.5^2) prior (see bm_prior(adjustment_sd = )): no pooling, no link and no extra hyperparameters. Formula random effects get one copy per part, replicated per feature. Residual variances by "vb"; compositional reference: the median over features, on joint posterior samples. Features without both presences and absences only enter the abundance part. With evaluate_only, "hierarchical" is used instead. Does not support ordered() yet.

  • "none": each feature on its own, with the median comparison on posterior draws for compositionality.

  • "hierarchical": one INLA model per part with all features. Without median comparison, beta_jk ~ N(0, tau_k^2); with it, beta_jk = mu_k + u_jk, u_jk ~ N(0, tau_k^2), with a PC prior on tau_k; see hierarchical_reference. Random effects are replicated per feature with shared variances. The Gaussian prior has no point mass at the reference, so lfsr controls sign errors, not point nulls. Does not support ordered() or link = "shared" yet; thresholds are not used.

exposure

With shrinkage = "joint", the variable(s) of interest: names of fixed-effect variables of the formula (for example "diagnosis"). Their coefficients get the full joint structure (link lambda to prevalence and information shared across features, two hyperparameters per coefficient); the other covariates are adjustment covariates with one effect per feature. Default: the first variable of the formula. To give every covariate the full structure, list them all. Not used by the other shrinkage options.

hierarchical_reference

Compositional reference used by shrinkage = "hierarchical" under median comparison:

  • "mean" (default): the latent common centre mu_k. The corrected effect is u_jk = beta_jk - mu_k, whose posterior marginal INLA gives directly.

  • "median": the median over features of beta_jk, computed on joint posterior samples. More robust when the true effects go mostly in one direction, which pulls mu_k away from the features with no effect.

hierarchical_variance

Residual variances of the abundance part with shrinkage = "hierarchical", one per feature:

  • "vb" (default): mean-field variational updates alternating with INLA. INLA fits the model given the current variances; each variance then gets a conjugate update from the INLA residuals (including their uncertainty and the random effects), with a common prior on the variances estimated from all features as in limma. Repeats until the precisions change by less than 1% (at most 10 INLA fits). No lm().

  • "plugin": estimated with lm() per feature (without the random effects) and passed to INLA as fixed weights; INLA only estimates a common multiplier. Fastest, but with random effects the relative variances are less accurate.

  • "estimated": one Gaussian likelihood per feature, so INLA estimates every precision with its uncertainty. Adds one hyperparameter per feature, which makes the fit much slower as the number of features grows; needs int_strategy = "eb" with many features.

int_strategy

How INLA integrates over the hyperparameters (INLA's int.strategy): "auto", "ccd", "grid" or "eb" (empirical Bayes: only the posterior mode of the hyperparameters, much faster with many of them). With shrinkage = "joint", "auto" means "eb": the model has several hyperparameters per coefficient, well estimated from all features, and integrating over them ("ccd") changes the results little but makes the final fit several times slower. Otherwise it applies to the hierarchical fits and to hierarchical_variance = "estimated".

median_comparison_abundance, median_comparison_prevalence

Compare each coefficient with the median of that coefficient across features instead of with zero, as in maaslin3(). This corrects for compositionality: with relative abundances, when some features increase the others appear to decrease. On by default for abundance, off for prevalence (as in MaAsLin3). The comparison is done on posterior draws, so lfsr, prob_positive and the q-values refer to coef - median; see Details.

median_comparison_abundance_threshold, median_comparison_prevalence_threshold

Minimum distance from the median for an effect to count, on the coefficient scale. With threshold t, lfsr = min(P(delta <= t), P(delta >= -t)) where delta = coef - median.

subtract_median

If TRUE, coef, stderr and the credible interval describe coef - median instead of the raw coefficient.

n_draws

Number of posterior draws per coefficient used for the median comparison (at most 1000 joint samples for "joint" and "hierarchical").

selection

Rule turning posteriors into qval_individual and qval_joint (and significant_results.tsv). Every rule is applied separately for each coefficient (e.g. diagnosisCD), so covariates with many associations do not lend discoveries to the others (MaAsLin3 pools all coefficients):

  • "bh_lfsr" (default): Benjamini-Hochberg on 2 * lfsr within each coefficient and model part; joint as MaAsLin3, pbeta(min(p), 1, 2) then BH. It kept the false discovery rate at the nominal level in simulations.

  • "rope": probability that the corrected effect is practically null, P(|effect| <= rope_delta), from a normal approximation of the posterior; q-value = running mean of the sorted probabilities (Bayesian FDR for relevant effects). Too liberal for features whose effects are not shrunk.

  • "lfsr": running mean of the sorted lfsr (Bayesian false sign rate). Too liberal when many features have no effect.

rope_delta

Half-width of the region of practical equivalence for selection = "rope", on the coefficient scale (0.5 on log2 is a 1.4-fold change).

save_models

Keep the INLA fit of every feature in the result.

cores

Number of threads used by INLA.

verbosity

"FINEST", "DEBUG" or "INFO" print progress (with shrinkage = "joint", also each "vb" iteration with its time, the final fit and the posterior sampling); any other value, such as "WARN", is quiet.

...

Other maaslin3() arguments. They are accepted for compatibility but not used yet; a warning lists them.

Value

An object of class bayome: a list with results (one row per feature, coefficient and model part), fits (INLA fits if save_models = TRUE), lambda (the estimated prevalence-abundance links, one per coefficient, with shrinkage = "joint"; otherwise NULL), the processed data and metadata, the INLA model specification and the settings. Results columns follow MaAsLin3 (feature, metadata, value, name, coef, stderr, qval_individual, qval_joint, error, model, N, N_not_zero): coef and stderr are the posterior mean and standard deviation, and the q-values follow selection (Benjamini-Hochberg on 2 * lfsr by default). With shrinkage = "joint" and save_models = TRUE, the fit is in fits$joint, with the estimated links in attr(fits$joint, "bm_lambda"). Extra columns: lower_95, upper_95 (95% credible interval), prob_positive (posterior probability that the effect is positive), lfsr and lfsr_joint (local false sign rates) and null_hypothesis (the posterior mean of the median used as reference; 0 when the coefficient was compared with zero).

Details

bayome fits a two-part (hurdle) model:

  • prevalence: presence/absence, binomial likelihood with logit link, using all samples;

  • abundance: transformed abundance (log2 of the normalised value by default), Gaussian likelihood, using only the samples where the feature is present.

By default (shrinkage = "joint") all features and both parts are fitted in one INLA model. Prevalence effects are estimated feature by feature; abundance effects are shrunk towards what each feature's prevalence effect suggests, u_A = lambda * u_P + e, with one lambda per covariate estimated from all features and e shared across features.

As in MaAsLin3, the pipeline is normalise, filter, transform, then fit.

Median comparison. For each coefficient (for example diagnosisCD) and posterior draw, the median across features is computed, and each feature's draw is compared with it: delta = beta - median. Features are fitted separately, so their posteriors are independent and the draws can be combined directly; the posterior of delta therefore includes the uncertainty of the median, and the fact that each feature contributes to it. Rows with an error, and coefficients present in fewer than three features, do not take part. Draws are random: call set.seed() first for reproducible results.

References

Nickols WA, Kuntz T, Shen J, Maharjan S, Mallick H, Franzosa EA, Thompson KN, Nearing JT, Huttenhower C (2026). MaAsLin 3: refining and extending generalized multivariable linear models for meta-omic association discovery. Nature Methods, 23, 554-564. doi:10.1038/s41592-025-02923-9
